What zumir has, and what runs here

Source: R/info.R
zumir_info.Rd

zumir_info() reports the vendored MIR, whether it has a code generator for this CPU, which tiers run in this session and why the others do not, and the memory MIR contexts hold. zumir_tier() is the tier code runs on by default.

Usage

zumir_info()

zumir_tier()

Value

zumir_info(): a list with

  • mir_commit: the upstream MIR commit vendored;

  • mir_patches: the local patches, one per element;

  • target: TRUE when MIR has a code generator for this CPU and was compiled in;

  • tier: as zumir_tier();

  • capabilities: a data frame with columns tier, capability, ok and reason (NA where ok);

  • memory: a list with contexts, the MIR contexts alive, and bytes, the memory they hold.

zumir_tier(): "native", "interp" or "none".

Details

At load, zumir compiles and calls a small function natively and on MIR's interpreter. Each tier is reported as four capabilities, which fail separately: compile (MIR builds the function on this tier), entry (it has an address C can call), run (calling it gives the right answer) and external (it can call a C library function, exp). A tier is available when all four hold.

Both tiers need memory that is writable and executable, the interpreter too, since MIR generates small call bridges for it. Where the system refuses that memory (SELinux deny_execmem, some seccomp policies and hardened containers), neither tier runs, and zumir_tier() is "none". The reason column says what was refused. On macOS, R needs the com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit entitlement that CRAN's build carries.

Examples

zumir_tier()
#> [1] "native"
info <- zumir_info()
info$capabilities
#>     tier capability   ok reason
#> 1 native    compile TRUE   <NA>
#> 2 native      entry TRUE   <NA>
#> 3 native        run TRUE   <NA>
#> 4 native   external TRUE   <NA>
#> 5 interp    compile TRUE   <NA>
#> 6 interp      entry TRUE   <NA>
#> 7 interp        run TRUE   <NA>
#> 8 interp   external TRUE   <NA>
